text: Tokens supply values; source components show how the brand uses them. Preserve that composition instead of reducing the brand to a palette.

loc: Resolve the source of design decisions
text: 1. Follow the user's current explicit requirements … 2. For a retained or adapted band, use its inspected source …: actual fonts, scale, backgrounds, product stage, crop, spacing and behavior. 3. Use the current Creative Brief and kit to guide new material and fill source gaps. … 4. Use generic design defaults only for properties with no applicable evidence.
A missing property stays unknown; do not invent a rule such as "one colored band per page" and impose it on captured originals.

loc: Preserve the background and media system
text: Record the observed sequence of surfaces, image fields and content density. A brand may use several vivid fields or a single canvas. Neither a universal alternating-band pattern nor a one-chromatic-peak limit applies to every brand. For a new band, inherit the relevant ancestor's treatment and the page's rhythm.
note: Site D2: "Choose brand-section surfaces so light and dark alternate." "Use at most one dark brand section."

loc: Preserve the background and media system
text: Use the source's imagery posture. A text-only band can remain text-only; every band need not have decorative art.
Read family, weight, size, line-height, tracking, text width and breakpoint behavior from the relevant source … An h1/h2 tag or platform type token alone does not guarantee the measured style.

Judge the page together, not each band in isolation. … An accidentally tiny opening headline beside a much larger ordinary product heading is a mismatch to fix … Preserve a deliberate source scale contrast; do not invent a one-large-heading quota for the brand.

Preserve observed button geometry, padding, type, border and contrast. … Select a variant that reads against the required surface before recoloring. Recolor only when necessary for contrast and within the brand's observed system.
Before a scoped change, record the current band's keeper properties and the specific defect. … Did the requested change improve its target without losing an existing strength?
